About

A CS student who prefers finished systems over finished tutorials.

Dipesh Kumar Panda
B.Tech CS Student · NIST Berhampur

I started with the fundamentals — C, C++, Java, Python — and moved quickly into building things people would actually use: a complaint-management platform with real role hierarchies, an AI-powered scholarship matcher, a book summarizer, and a campus waste-tracking system.

What I care about most is the gap between "it works on my machine" and "it works for five different user roles under real deadlines." That's the gap I chase in every project — SLA escalation logic, authentication edge cases, database schemas that don't fall apart at scale.

Outside of coursework, I'm sharpening problem-solving through competitive aptitude practice (AINCAT) and exploring AI-assisted development workflows with tools like agentic IDEs and LLM APIs.

Featured Work

Projects built to be used, not just demoed

Four systems spanning full-stack web, mobile, and AI-assisted tooling — each solving a real, specific problem.

01Full-Stack

Smart Campus Complaint Management System

ExpressTypeScriptSequelizeMySQLReactViteTailwind CSSRender

A production complaint-management platform built for NIST University, handling the full lifecycle of a complaint across five distinct user roles — student, faculty, staff, department head, and admin.

  • Designed a role-based access system so each user type sees only what's relevant to them, from filing a complaint to resolving one.
  • Built an automatic SLA escalation engine — complaints that miss their resolution window escalate on their own, paired with real-time alerts.
  • Shipped an admin analytics dashboard tracking open complaints, resolution rates, and escalation trends by department.
  • Diagnosed and fixed a live authentication race condition and several route-security gaps, maintaining a Postman collection for regression testing.
GitHub ↗
02Mobile · AI

AI Scholarship Suggestion App

FlutterAI APIMySQLMongoDB

A matching engine that reads a student's academic record and demographic profile, then surfaces scholarships they can realistically qualify for — instead of a generic, unfiltered list.

  • Built an AI-driven eligibility check that filters out scholarships the student doesn't actually qualify for.
  • Added category filters and automated deadline alerts so students don't miss application windows.
  • Designed the data layer across MySQL and MongoDB to handle structured eligibility rules alongside flexible scholarship metadata.
GitHub ↗
03Web · AI

AI Book Summarizer

HTMLCSSJavaScriptAI API

A web tool that turns an uploaded PDF or pasted text into a structured, chapter-by-chapter summary instead of one undifferentiated block of text.

  • Breaks long-form content into chapters, each with its own key points and takeaways.
  • Generates an optional auto quiz so users can check comprehension without leaving the page.
  • Integrated directly with an AI API for summarization, with no server-side dependency required.
GitHub ↗
04Web · DBMS

Waste Management System

HTMLCSSJavaScriptDBMS

A campus web application for logging and monitoring waste collection at NIST University, backed by a relational database for reporting.

  • Built simple, focused screens for submitting waste reports, tagging categories, and tracking pickup status.
  • Structured the database schema to support ongoing reporting on collection trends.
GitHub ↗
05Web · Game

Spin & Win — Gamified Rewards Wheel

JavaScriptHTML5 CanvasCSS AnimationsLocalStorage

A lightweight, embeddable spin-the-wheel widget for driving engagement on landing pages — configurable prize slots, weighted odds, and zero backend dependency.

  • Built the wheel and spin physics on HTML5 Canvas, with easing-based deceleration so every spin feels natural rather than mechanically linear.
  • Implemented a weighted-probability engine so site owners can set real win odds per prize slot instead of a flat random draw.
  • Used LocalStorage to enforce a one-spin-per-user cooldown, preventing repeat spins without needing a server or login.
  • Exposed a small config object (prize labels, colors, odds, cooldown window) so the whole widget can be re-skinned and redeployed on a new page in minutes.
